asA: operator finalising one build unit on a tree that carries hundreds of acceptance criteria
iWant: `rcf build finalise <fbs-id>` to verify only the acceptance criteria bound to that FBS by default, with `rcf verify run --fbs <id>` as the underlying filter and an explicit `--all` option that restores whole-chain verification
soThat: finalising one build unit costs one unit's verification rather than the whole chain, the ADR-4112 verified invariant still holds per FBS (every AC bound to the FBS verified, none skipped), and a whole-chain run stays available at slice end
title: US-16504: finalise verifies one build unit by default; whole-chain verification on request

acceptanceCriteria.description: rcf verify run accepts an FBS filter (--fbs <id>, repeatable) and verifies exactly the acceptance criteria bound to those FBS items; the report states the scope and the AC count.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a chain whose FBS items bind disjoint sets of acceptance criteria
acceptanceCriteria.when: rcf verify run --repo <chain> --fbs <fbs-id> ... is invoked (the option is repeatable), in agent mode or deterministic mode
acceptanceCriteria.then: the verifier is briefed on exactly the acceptance criteria bound to the named FBS items and no others; the report records run.scope as 'fbs:<ids>' and run.scopeAcCount as the number of criteria in scope; in deterministic mode run.runStats.counts.total equals that number; an unknown FBS id refuses with exit 2 and names the id; a run without --fbs records run.scope 'chain' and behaves as before

acceptanceCriteria.description: rcf build finalise <fbs-id> passes its FBS as the verify filter by default; --all restores whole-chain verification.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an FBS at status 'complete' bound to a subset of the chain's acceptance criteria
acceptanceCriteria.when: rcf build finalise <fbs-id> --url ... is invoked without --all, and separately with --all
acceptanceCriteria.then: without --all the fresh rcf verify run subprocess receives --fbs <fbs-id> and the finalise output names the scope and the AC count; with --all no --fbs filter is passed and the whole chain is verified; the promotion to 'verified' still requires a passing run with ship authority
acceptanceCriteria.supersessionNote: Retired 2026-10-26 (stage-keeper ruling RC-10, round A ruling 5: retired and succeeded, never reworded): Finalise never spawns anything but git (AC-20002-5), so it launches no verify run and writes no verify report.

acceptanceCriteria.description: The ADR-4112 verified invariant is evaluated over the scoped AC set: a skipped AC inside the scope refuses promotion, a skipped AC outside the scope does not, and an FBS with zero bound ACs is refused with a plain message.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a chain where one FBS binds an acceptance criterion the verifier cannot exercise (it lands on blockedAcs) and another FBS binds only exercisable criteria
acceptanceCriteria.when: rcf build finalise is run for each FBS in turn, and for an FBS whose acIds list is empty
acceptanceCriteria.then: the FBS whose scoped set contains the skipped criterion is refused (exit 4, left at 'complete') with a line naming the unexercised criteria and ADR-4112, in agent mode and deterministic mode alike; the FBS whose scoped set contains no skipped criterion is promoted when the run passes with ship authority; an FBS with zero bound acceptance criteria is refused before verify launches (exit 3, the schema forbids an empty binding) with a plain message naming the FBS and saying there is nothing to verify

acceptanceCriteria.description: The help text for finalise and verify run, the human report render and the finalise docs page describe the verification scope plainly.
acceptanceCriteria.when: rcf build finalise --help, rcf verify run --help, rcf verify report <path> and the finalise docs page are read
acceptanceCriteria.then: each states plainly that finalise verifies the named FBS's bound acceptance criteria by default, that --all verifies the whole chain, and that verify run --fbs <id> is the filter; the human report render shows the scope and the AC count
